cells.tense: You are inside your own thinking at a depth that feels settled today.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: After a page of thinking you care about, sit with it five quiet minutes — no edits, no additions, no explaining it to yourself.
cells.core:
Some of what you make comes out of a depth you can't fully account for. You know what it means before you can put the meaning into words. Where the making is going well, that's most of the thing — the words land, the structure holds, and the reasoning is almost an afterthought, there to explain what you already knew.

You can walk to the edge of your own knowing and leave the last unnamed part alone, without filling it in. Pick a piece of thinking you care about and sit with it five quiet minutes once it's finished. No edits, no additions, no explaining it to yourself. What's yours stays yours that way — the depth keeps its own order and you get to notice what you actually made in the first place.
cells.sheetLine: You can let the deepest part go unnamed and still trust it.
cells.verb: going so deep into a pattern that the thinking runs out and only knowing is left
cells.place: a threshold where what you are is becoming visible without being arranged

cells.tense: You are rushing toward the finished meaning before the thing has found its own shape.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: When a plan forms, give the others one clear sentence about how it should go, then stop — no defending it, no filling the quiet after.
cells.core:
The pull to arrive is fast now. You're at a depth where the whole structure of a thing shows up at once, and the urgency is to hand it to someone finished, explained and closed before it can be questioned. Those on the other side of the table can get a certainty they didn't ask for and can't join in on.

Give the order of things in one sentence, plainly, and then stop. One line about how it should go, out loud, without arguing for it afterward. If the read is off, you've spent a pause and learned something; nothing was risked that can't be undone. What comes back in the quiet tells you whether the frame was yours or only yours to hold, and whether anyone wants to take it up with you.
cells.sheetLine: You know how it should go. Give the one line, then stop.

cells.place: a threshold where what you are is becoming visible without being arranged

cells.tense: You went somewhere with your thinking and have not come back from it yet.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: When something you work out actually pleases you, name it out loud to someone that same day, before the warmth goes.
cells.core:
There's a piece of work with your whole mind in it, and you've stopped short of bringing it out where people can see it. The depth is real and it's still there. What's missing is any signal that the thing you found matters — to anyone but you.

When something you work out actually pleases you, one person hears about it that day, in plain words, before you've talked yourself out of it. Not a report — just the good thing, from you, while it's warm. If the read of this space is off, saying one good thing out loud teaches you the same amount either way, and the pleasure gets somewhere to go besides back into the work. It was already yours to say.

cells.tense: Something has been receding from you quietly, gently, and you keep not deciding about it.
cells.act: let the feeling settle into its own depth
cells.ask: This week, sit with a thing you care about for twenty minutes with no task attached, and notice where the quiet leads.
cells.core:
There's a place you're not going back to, or a way you've been making things that thinned out without you marking it. You live nearer that edge than you let on, and the distance started small — an evening skipped, a message not answered — and it's been getting easier each time. Ask what's ending and you'd say nothing is. There's a good chance the leaving has been in your hands and unsigned.

Sit down for twenty minutes with a thing you care about and no task attached, and stop when you stop. Notice whether the quiet that follows feels like yours. If it doesn't, you've learned where you actually are, and no harm was done. If it does, you found something that was waiting for you to claim it — and you can mark it as yours, or not.

attempts.check: The weakest claim is the Unacknowledged cell's 'by your hand:' the kernel says authorship is misattributed, not that the person is deliberately half-releasing anything, so I've softened it to a leaving they keep not deciding about. A reader could reasonably say the Too Much cell rules on how others experience them, so I kept it to what can be observed at the table. The asks survive being wrong because each is small and reversible: a page checked and left, a frame put down and reclaimed, one line answered out loud. The sentence serving me most is the slow near-oracle opener about the last where before the why — I've aimed it at a week, not at a person.
